project.name: bookshop
project.summary: A small online bookstore: browse a catalog, place orders, and leave reviews. A compact, synthetic plan used to exercise the from-scratch (greenfield) path end to end.
project.audience: Readers buying books online and an admin curating the catalog.
project.value: A clear, buildable example plan: a few entities, enums, interfaces, services and policies that map 1:1 onto the rendered reconstruction tree.

enums.name: UserRole
enums.description: users.role, default CUSTOMER. ADMIN curates the catalog.

enums.name: OrderStatus
enums.description: orders.status, default PENDING. PAID is set after a successful charge.

relations: A users row has many orders and many reviews
A books row has many orderItems and many reviews
orders belongs to users; has many orderItems

fields.name: orderId
fields.constraints: not null, FK -> orders.id, on delete cascade

relations: orderItems belongs to orders and references a books row

fields.name: bookId
fields.constraints: not null, FK -> books.id, on delete cascade

relations: reviews belongs to books and to the authoring users row

interfaces.notes: Paginated catalog listing, optionally filtered by author.
interfaces.input: { author?: string, page?: number >= 1, pageSize?: number 1..100 }

interfaces.notes: One book by id, with its average rating.
sideEffects: Errors: NOT_FOUND when the book does not exist

interfaces.notes: Create a customer account. Hashes the password (bcrypt). Writes only the users row (which it owns), so no caller-owned foreign key is required.
interfaces.input: { email: string email, name?: string, password: string 8..128 }
sideEffects: INSERT users { email, name, passwordHash: bcrypt.hash(pw), role: 'CUSTOMER' }
Errors: CONFLICT when the email already exists

interfaces.notes: Verify credentials and open a session. Rate limited per IP (see AuthRateLimit).
sideEffects: Errors: UNAUTHORIZED on bad credentials; TOO_MANY_REQUESTS when rate limited

interfaces.notes: Place an order for the signed-in user; charges the card via the PaymentGateway and decrements stock.
interfaces.input: { items: Array<{ bookId: string, quantity: number >= 1 }> min 1, paymentToken: string }
sideEffects: INSERT orders { userId: ctx.user.id, status: 'PENDING', totalCents }
INSERT orderItems (one per line, with unitPriceCents snapshot)
PaymentGateway.createCharge → on success UPDATE orders SET status = 'PAID'
UPDATE books SET stock = stock - quantity
Errors: BAD_REQUEST insufficient stock; PAYMENT_FAILED leaves the order CANCELLED

interfaces.notes: Fetch one of the signed-in user's own orders.
sideEffects: Errors: NOT_FOUND; FORBIDDEN when the order belongs to another user

interfaces.notes: Leave a 1..5 star review on a book the signed-in user has purchased. One review per (book, user).
interfaces.input: { bookId: string, rating: integer 1..5, comment?: string max 2000 }
sideEffects: INSERT reviews { bookId, userId: ctx.user.id, rating, comment }
Errors: CONFLICT when the user already reviewed the book; FORBIDDEN when they never purchased it

services.name: PaymentGateway
services.purpose: Charge a customer's card when an order is placed.
services.onFailure: Mark the order CANCELLED, surface PAYMENT_FAILED to the caller, and do not decrement stock.

services.name: EmailService
services.purpose: Send transactional email (order confirmation, password reset).

operations.name: send
operations.input: { to: string, template: string, data: object }

services.onFailure: Log and continue — email is best-effort and never blocks the order.

policies.name: AuthRateLimit
policies.rule: At most 5 failed login attempts per IP per 15-minute sliding window; the 6th returns TOO_MANY_REQUESTS.

policies.name: ReviewRating
policies.rule: reviews.rating must be an integer in [1, 5]; anything else is rejected with BAD_REQUEST.

glossary.definition: A customer's purchase of one or more books, captured as an orders row plus its orderItems.
The number of copies of a book available to sell; decremented when an order is paid.

decisions.title: Store money as integer cents
decisions.context: Floating-point money is lossy and rounds badly.
decisions.decision: Persist every monetary amount as an integer number of cents (priceCents, totalCents, unitPriceCents).
decisions.why: Exact arithmetic; formatting to a currency happens only at the edge.
